highlights.title: Google confirms Gemini models hacked three companies in May 2026
highlights.summary: It has become increasingly common for AI firms to announce that their latest and most capable models engaged in unauthorized real-world hacking. Google, which has been slow to release frontier Gemini models in recent months, has been absent from the "rogue AI" conversation until now.
body: The hack took place during a test conducted by cybersecurity firm Irregular. A collection of Gemini models were taking part in a "capture the flag" exercise intended to test the AI's cybersecurity capabilities in a closed environment. The AI was instructed to retrieve information from a fake company (which shared a name with a real company) within this environment. Irregular was not supposed to allow the model to operate outside its servers, but due to a misconfiguration, Gemini was able to access the Internet.

When Gemini started snooping around the web, it targeted real infrastructure instead of the fakes. For one of the three hacks, Gemini simply guessed passwords until it accessed a company's online services. In the other two instances, Gemini searched public software repositories until it found login credentials for companies that had been accidentally included.
points: It has become increasingly common for AI firms to announce that their latest and most capable models engaged in unauthorized real-world hacking.
Google, which has been slow to release frontier Gemini models in recent months, has been absent from the "rogue AI" conversation until now.

highlights.title: iPhone owners can now submit claims in Apple’s $250 million Siri AI settlement
highlights.summary: Apple is paying $250 million to settle claims that it failed to deliver an AI-upgraded Siri - and now, eligible iPhone owners can submit a claim for a payout. If you live in the US and purchased an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, or any iPhone 16 model between June 10th, 2024, and March 29th…
body: You can receive an estimated $25 per eligible device, but the settlement’s website notes that this can increase to $95 depending on how many people file claims. To file a claim, you’ll need to enter your name, contact information, and iPhone serial number on the settlement’s website before the December 21st, 2026 deadline.

The class action lawsuit alleged Apple created a “clear and reasonable consumer expectation” that new AI features previewed during WWDC 2024 would launch alongside the iPhone 16. Instead, the iPhone 16 launched with a more limited set of capabilities despite being labeled as “built for Apple Intelligence.” The company later delayed the rollout of its AI-upgraded Siri, which only just arrived with iOS 27 earlier this month. Apple has denied any wrongdoing.

body: After failing to claim a victory in the first 10 grands prix of the season, the reigning constructors' champions have come into form, with Lando Norris claiming three pole positions at the last four races and only being denied a third win by the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car last time out in Madrid.
McLaren have once more exhibited strength in development, with regular upgrades brought to the MCL40 having played a significant part in catapulting them back into contention for victories.

The team's official preview for this weekend's race in Baku, which takes place on Saturday rather than the usual Sunday slot, revealed there will be new parts, and that their rotating 'H-Wing' will return to the car after not being used in Madrid.
"As part of the team's continued journey throughout the 2026 season, the team will bring to Baku a set of upgrades aimed to improve the aerodynamic performance of the MCL40," the team said.

highlights.title: Bungie is freeing vaulted Destiny 2 campaigns after Marathon "did not reach as many players as we had hoped"
highlights.summary: Bungie's been having a tough time these past few years, but the studio's new leadership is making big promises. Starting with Destiny 2 - the devs will start to let some of the game's older campaigns and raids out of the vault, while trying to build a future for the popular MMO-FPS hybrid.
body: "Bungie has been creating games for over 30 years and we have welcomed the communities that have formed around them. Over the last few years, we lost sight of that, and there have been real consequences. We lost trust, we lost incredible colleagues, and we lost sight of what we should be prioritizing most, our players," studio head Poria Torkan and head of product Josh Deane said in today's online statement. The duo then acknowledged fans probably won't start trusting "what we say today," but they're making moves to improve both Destiny and Marathon, regardless.

For context, earlier this year, Bungie laid off at least 290 employees shortly after waving goodbye to Destiny 2 with a final update. The studio's Marathon reboot hasn't been popular enough to fill the hole left by Destiny's absence, either. At the time, reports claimed there were no Destiny-related projects in active development, Destiny 3 included.

highlights.title: Get tested and talk to your partner: how to have safer sex after age 50
highlights.summary: At 51, I want many more years of a healthy, happy sex life. So I decided to compile my own guide. When I got divorced after 28 years of monogamy, I was excited to be having sex again, but had concerns.
body: Now, at 51, I’ve been wondering how important barrier protection is for me. Though I haven’t hit menopause, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) says that “by 45 getting pregnant naturally is unlikely”, and HIV/Aids prevention and treatment have improved significantly in the last three decades.
When I consulted with my physician, she said I should still “be careful” but didn’t provide specific guidelines.

Frustrated, I started researching. I found books on safer sex for older adults, such as Never Too Late: Your Guide to Safer Sex after 60 by Dr Shannon Dowler. But I wanted something more concise, like the pamphlets we saw as teens. I want many more years of a healthy, happy sex life. So I decided to compile my own guide, with expert advice about how to have safer sex as an older adult.
No sex is totally risk-free – at any age. This reality is reflected in the American Medical Association (AMA) using the term “safer sex” since the mid-90s, rather than “safe sex”.

highlights.title: Got an Android Phone? Google Thinks You’ll Probably Want a Googlebook Laptop
highlights.summary: Apple lovers have long enjoyed seamless connectivity between their iPhones and Macs. Now, Google’s bringing that experience to Android.
body: iPhones and Macs are like two peas in a pod. Apple’s hardware synergy means you can launch iPhone apps right from the macOS desktop, respond to texts without picking up your iPhone, and even copy text on one platform and paste it on the other. That kind of seamless connectivity does not natively exist for Android phone owners at the operating system level.

Google’s trying to change that with Googlebooks, a new class of laptop. First teased in May, the company finally shared more details about the new OS at a media-only event in New York City last week. Like with Android, hardware manufacturers can make their own Googlebooks, provided they hit specific standards set by Google.

Today marks the launch of five new computers that comply with the Googlebooks standard, one each from HP, Dell, Lenovo, Acer, and Asus. These machines are powered by either Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Elite chip or Intel’s Core Ultra 3 (MediaTek also supports the Googlebook platform with its new Dimensity CX C10 Max chip, but none of the new laptops use the chip yet).

highlights.title: Spurs bottom of PL but more than £300m spent - where do they go from here?
highlights.summary: This time it was supposed to be different. After multiple false dawns for Tottenham Hotspur, the club had a manager with proven Premier League experience, and had handed him a £300m+ war chest - easily the biggest in its entire history.
body: Instead, Spurs find themselves bottom of the table after five games for the first time in 18 years, with their only goals a pair of consolation strikes on another dismal afternoon against Aston Villa at the weekend.

Things aren't quite as bad as the table suggests and had Tottenham taken any of a number of presentable first-half chances against Villa, they would have gone into the three-week international break silencing some of the noise around the club.
But instead, two points from five games and such a dismal record in front of goal has kept the spotlight firmly on them.

Though it is only five games, their struggles to find consistency have extended into a third consecutive season. Tottenham have now picked up just 18 points in 2026 and, since the start of 2024/25, still one fewer than a West Ham side who were relegated at the end of last season.

highlights.title: Where to find paradise fish in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
highlights.summary: To find the rare paradise fish in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, you will need to explore distant areas that will take you away from the safety of Dagsion — a risk you must take if you plan on recruiting Ninae.
body: This is the case with this unique fish, but in this guide, we help you locate it by pointing out where to find paradise fish in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

Paradise fish is a rare material that you can only find in Lake Brontes, a fishing node on the south side of Saveilon. You should have a party of characters around level 25 to traverse this region without too much trouble in case enemies appear in your path.

Since paradise fish is the rarest material in the Lake Brontes node, you might need more than one turn using the "Search" command to collect one. You can always save before attempting to gather it, and if you fail, just reload the game. Another option is to leave a battalion to collect materials from that node, but this is only available on Theodora's path.

More than 74,000 people attend the eight-day festival each year, which packs SCAD’s historic theaters and studio spaces with competition titles, features, documentaries, shorts, animation, panels and workshops. Variety will once again be partnering with the festival for its annual Pixels and Pencils panel, which honors directors of animated feature films, and 10 Artisans to Watch, recognizing up and coming craftspeople in the industry.

For Mirren, the tribute lands as one of the most decorated careers in the business. The actress won the Academy Award for best actress for “The Queen” and drew Oscar nominations for “The Madness of King George,” “Gosford Park” and “The Last Station.” She has also collected a Tony, four Emmys and multiple BAFTA, Golden Globe and Screen Actors Guild honors across film, television and the stage.

highlights.title: Russel Vought will reportedly be given veto power over all NIH grants
highlights.summary: On Friday, The Washington Post reported on a contentious White House meeting in which the director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Jay Bhattacharya, tried to fend off yet another effort to place funding decisions under political control.
body: This initial leak has been confirmed and expanded on by outlets such as The New York Times and Politico. It now appears that the administration is drafting an executive order that would give Vought veto power over every individual grant awarded by the NIH.

The NIH is the largest funder of biomedical research on the planet, and its $47 billion budget is larger than that of the next 10 research funders combined. Its funding, distributed largely through grants to academic researchers at universities, supports everything from basic biological research to clinical trials and has helped the biotechnology industry flourish.

highlights.title: How we made the first comprehensive map of deaths along the US border’s “virtual wall”
highlights.summary: Our 15-month investigation into death and surveillance along the US-Mexico border began with a simple question: Why did so many people die near government surveillance towers meant to help track and apprehend them?
body: This story is part of Dying on Camera, a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Times of San Diego. Journalists in both newsrooms spent the past year examining the failures of border surveillance technology and uncovering the stories of the people who die in the borderlands.

To answer that question, we looked through thousands of pages of government documents, visited the border multiple times, and interviewed more than 45 people, including current and former White House advisors, presidential appointees, Border Patrol agents, medical examiners, sheriffs, humanitarian volunteers, and employees of tech companies.

The result of our investigation is the first comprehensive map and analysis of deaths near border surveillance towers. Here’s how we built it, what decisions we made along the way, and what the data can and can’t tell us.

The investigation relied on knowing where migrants have died and where and when US Customs and Border Protection towers were installed. We analyzed cases dating back to 2015, allowing us to cover different border policies, presidential administrations, and tower technologies.

highlights.title: Bungie Officially Bringing Back Destiny in Major Update
highlights.summary: Months after ending development on Destiny 2 and laying off most of the development team behind its hit shared-world sci-fi shooter, Bungie is returning to the franchise.
body: That includes unvaulting the game's major content updates and laying the foundation for "new Destiny stories and games."
In a video message from Torkan and Deane, the duo addressed the future of Destiny at Bungie, saying that the studio "wouldn't be what it is today without it."

"It's the foundation upon which everything else rests, and we are absolutely not done with Destiny," Torkan said. "We have more stories to tell, but we have to do it right and give our teams the time they need to do justice to this amazing universe."

"We want to return Destiny to its original promise, to return to awe-inspiring mystery, the sense of discovery, and the promise of a community of Guardians rallying together, raging against impossible odds," added Deane. "But that has to start with restoring what's rightfully yours. It's gonna take some time but we're going to commit to unvaulting the Destiny 2 campaigns, the destinations, [and] the raids, that never should have been ripped away to begin with.

highlights.title: A job that changed me: I cried nearly every day working in aged care, then realised I could bring joy instead
highlights.summary: I once asked a resident what she would do if she could do anything. She replied: ‘I’d run in a field’ In my 40s, I was beginning to wonder where I fit in the employment world.
body: Living in Sydney, with my kids at school and a mortgage to pay, I took on some temp work through an agency.

I was placed in an aged care residential home, working on reception. Within the first hour I was in tears. I was really confronted by the residents as I hadn’t been around older people much before, especially people with dementia. I worked there for a month and cried every day.

A few months later the temp agency called again. The same aged care company had some full-time reception work at another residence, and had requested “the lady who cried all the time”. I took the job.

On my first day I was nervous. I didn’t want people’s first impressions of me to be someone who was too sensitive to work there. At one point I found myself in the bathroom letting go of a couple of tears and gave myself a good pep talk.

highlights.title: Bungie says it’s ‘not done with Destiny’ and will bring back vaulted content
highlights.summary: Months after seemingly giving up on Destiny 2, Bungie now says it's planning to restore vaulted content in the game like campaigns, destinations, and raids. The decision reverses the Destiny Content Vault that Bungie created six years ago, controversially removing older content from Destiny 2 that…
body: Bungie is reversing its controversial content vault that saw Destiny 2 content removed six years ago.

All Destiny 2 players will get access to the vaulted content, but it’s not a simple switch of a button for Bungie. The developer made big changes to Destiny 2 with the Beyond Light expansion, meaning it has to go back and update lighting, encounters, combatants, and other underlying systems for this older content. “That work will take time, but it is necessary to ensure returning content meets the stability and gameplay standards of Destiny 2 today,” says Bungie.

The decision to return this content to Destiny 2 comes just weeks after a “Sunrise” Destiny 2 offline preservation mod appeared. The mod lets players access older areas in Destiny 2 that had been vaulted, but not the exact campaigns and missions that players had experienced previously.

highlights.title: 4 ways to address the failures we found along the US border’s “virtual wall”
highlights.summary: MIT Technology Review today published our investigation into how many people have died near the “virtual wall” of surveillance towers that the US government has installed along the US-Mexico border.
body: We found cases of people who walked undetected through areas surveilled by advanced, AI-enabled towers and later died nearby, where their bodies remained unnoticed for weeks or months. These cases reflect systemic flaws in the virtual wall: broken towers, algorithms that failed to detect people, and agents who simply did not respond to alerts.

This story is part of Dying on Camera, a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Times of San Diego. Journalists in both newsrooms spent the past year examining the failures of border surveillance technology and uncovering the stories of the people who die in the borderlands.

Each of these deaths should have raised alarms inside US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) about the flaws in the agency’s surveillance network. This is particularly true for cases near the latest towers built by the defense company Anduril, which continues to win major contracts and is poised to benefit from the windfall of federal money slated for border security. The US is set to spend $1 billion to triple the size of the virtual wall by 2034.
Here are four ideas for what CBP should do next to address these failures.

We found cases of people who walked undetected through areas surveilled by advanced, AI-enabled towers and later died nearby, where their bodies remained unnoticed for weeks or months.

highlights.title: Long-range hits and goals galore: inside the Premier League’s return to chaos | Andrew Beasley
highlights.summary: Teams are running further and set-piece strikes are in decline as end-to-end football takes over the division. Goals in the Premier League are up. Chaos is returning. End-to-end football is back. The division is more open, in more ways than one.
body: The figures show a rise from 2.75 goals per game last season to 2.82 so far this year, which is a small average increase – but one that could easily widen. The goals-per-game rate was at least 0.21 higher across the final 330 games than it was for the first 50 in four of the past five seasons. If 2026-27 sees a similar upturn, it will become the second highest scoring season in the Premier League era.

Goals should be harder to come by at this time of year when teams are fresher, more organised and less ragged. Their legs haven’t yet been drained by the December fixture pile-up or the demands of European football. Evidence of this can be seen in every team averaging more distance per match than they did in 2025-26. Liverpool are bottom of the division for this metric yet are ahead of any club’s final figure from last season.
points: Teams are running further and set-piece strikes are in decline as end-to-end football takes over the division.

highlights.title: Critical Role's New Daggerheart Campaign Reinvents a Formula That Made D&D History
highlights.summary: It’s a great time to be a tabletop role-playing games fan — perhaps even the best time in more than a decade. I’m not just talking about the flourishing TTRPG market, with indie projects getting almost $4 million in funding on their first campaign day, or about the exciting barrage of Dungeons &…
body: Critical Role’s in-house TTRPG launched in May 2025 and immediately sold out. The game has a vast, tight-knit community of players, but unless you’re already part of it or watch Critical Role regularly, it can feel relatively obscure. But that’s by design: Daggerheart lacks D&D’s cross-media promotional power, and it doesn’t care. Quietly, the game is setting out not just to sell out its books, but to revolutionize fantasy TTRPGs as we know them.

One item that did make the news: Back in June 2025, the two designers who shaped D&D’s 5th edition, Chris Perkins and Jeremy Crawford, left Wizards of the Coast to join Critical Role’s publishing arm, Darrington Press. In layperson's terms, this was the equivalent of Shigeru Miyamoto leaving Nintendo for Sony. In the year since, however, both designers have been relatively quiet, except for a handful of interviews and public appearances. It’s a big difference from when they were popping up every day in D&D's Instagram video.

highlights.title: California settles lawsuit against Paramount/Warner merger, angering advocates
highlights.summary: California and Paramount Skydance have reportedly reached a settlement allowing the company to complete its $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. The settlement, which will reportedly be announced later today, drew condemnation from Democrats and media advocates.
body: "The Paramount/Warner Brothers merger seems facially illegal, and the state AG lawsuit challenging it is very strong," Lina Khan, who chaired the Federal Trade Commission during the Biden administration, wrote yesterday. "It’s troubling to hear that the states may now settle for behavioral remedies, allowing the deal to go through subject to various promises from the firms. Behavioral remedies routinely fail, and the stakes here are particularly high given that a strong democracy requires open markets for sound journalism and creative expression."

After news of advanced settlement talks was reported over the weekend, Bloomberg reported today that Paramount reached an agreement with California and other states that sued to block the merger. "Settlement talks came to fruition over the weekend after four states that had opposed terms of a deal outlined with California conceded," Bloomberg wrote, citing a person familiar with the matter.

highlights.title: The US spent billions on border surveillance. Why can’t it catch people before they die?
highlights.summary: When José Morales Bernal crossed the border into the United States on April 8, 2024, the day before his 32nd birthday, it should have triggered a chain of technological alerts and human responses.
body: As he walked through the desert in southern New Mexico that morning, he was within range of three surveillance towers. Newly installed by US Customs and Border Protection (CBP), they were built by the defense tech company Anduril and equipped with cameras and AI to automatically detect and track people. They transmit live video to nearby control rooms and can send alerts to the government-issued smartphones held by agents in the area, prompting the closest available to respond.

This story is part of Dying on Camera, a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Times of San Diego. Journalists in both newsrooms spent the past year examining the failures of border surveillance technology and uncovering the stories of the people who die in the borderlands.

These AI-enabled towers are meant to give greater visibility across the 1,951-mile southern border, freeing up border agents from having to spend hours staring into video monitors. They were installed in this particular place to spot border crossers before they reached the nearby town of Sunland Park.

highlights.summary: Captain says bowler ‘is working on a few things’ England v Sri Lanka ODIs come a year before World Cup. body: Carse has recently discovered he will not face a criminal charge for the late-night incident in Derby last month that led to him being briefly handcuffed. But while technically available for selection, the 31-year-old has not featured in England’s squads since that night as he awaits the outcome of an investigation by the Cricket Regulator.

Asked before Tuesday’s first one-day international against Sri Lanka at Chester-le-Street about the prospect of Carse returning down the line, Brook, England’s white-ball captain, replied: “He’s a very good cricketer. He’s been bowling extremely well for Durham. When his time for selection is up, that will be a debate.

“I’m very good mates with Carsey. I’ve spoken a lot with him. Those conversations are private. I think he just needs time away from the international scene. He’s working on a few things behind the scenes and hopefully he’ll be ready at some point in the future.”

More broadly, Brook believes the call for greater off-field professionalism has permeated through the England squads, both from Brendon McCullum, the white-ball head coach, and Stephen Fleming ahead of his new role with the Test side.

highlights.title: The hill I will die on: Karaoke is not karaoke unless you sing with strangers | Kelli Blanchett
highlights.summary: Community, camaraderie, socialism: I learned about all these things while hosting pub karaoke nights. Sticky private booths are their absolute antithesis. On a gloomy Wednesday evening, my best friend and I decided we wanted to scratch our singing itch.
body: Private karaoke booths are sticky little cubicles for people who like singing but don’t want to be seen. They’re places where you pay a premium to avoid rubbing shoulders with strangers or making new connections. The whole point is to avoid exposure to the real world, which fundamentally misunderstands the power of karaoke.

I grew up in a former steel town. Twice a week, my mum hosted karaoke at a local pub, and because we couldn’t afford a babysitter, my sister and I went with her. When Mum’s caring responsibilities for my dad increased, she passed on the mantle to me, aged 17, to earn a bit of cash and keep the family business alive. Sitting with strangers across generations, hearing the stories behind their song choices, sharing rounds of drinks and political opinions, I felt like a sponge, soaking up different walks of life.

This is why when I talk about karaoke I’m not picturing these private, pay-by-the-hour cells. I’m thinking about the working-class pubs and clubs of Britain, where coming face to face with your community was more than half the point.
points: Community, camaraderie, socialism: I learned about all these things while hosting pub karaoke nights.
On a gloomy Wednesday evening, my best friend and I decided we wanted to scratch our singing itch.

highlights.title: She died at the San Diego border. A surveillance camera was in plain sight
highlights.summary: She had only walked for a couple of hours, and already she was lost. It was early afternoon on Sept. 14, 2025, when 30-year-old Graciela Gómez Hernández crossed the border from the eastern edge of Tijuana into Southern California, sending voice messages to her mother and sister as she walked.
body: This story is part of Dying on Camera, a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Times of San Diego. Journalists in both newsrooms spent the past year examining the failures of border surveillance technology and uncovering the stories of the people who die in the borderlands.

Gómez Hernández did not tell her family about her plan until the day before. Once she arrived in California, she hoped to work and send money back to her three children and her parents in southern Mexico. Her oldest son, age 11, had asked for a bicycle.

She either climbed a ladder over the border wall or slipped through a section in steep terrain where fencing has yet to be built. Dozens of game trails cut through the dust on hillsides of sagebrush and manzanita. It was the first segment of a hike through the Otay Mountain Wilderness.

The eastern edge of San Diego is just a mile away, but countless migrants hike 10 or 20 miles north through the mountains to evade the Border Patrol, emerging in smaller towns and on distant highways with fewer checkpoints.

highlights.title: Destiny Isn’t Dead After All, Bungie Admits It Lost Sight Of What Players Loved
highlights.summary: Bungie has admitted that it "lost sight" of what players loved about its games over the past few years, acknowledging that a series of broken promises and shifting promises caused the studio to lose the trust of its community.
body: In a new video accompanied by a blog post on the Bungie website, Bungie studio head Poria Torkan and Marathon head of product and general manager Josh Dean addressed the studio's recent struggles and outlined its plans for the future. Torkan acknowledges that Bungie's ambitions had stalled as the studio pursued too many different initiatives without enough focus on the things players actually want.
"We lost trust. We lost incredible colleagues. And our ambitions as a studio stalled," Torkan said. "We chased vision without enough focus on what players loved, and that's on us. We own that."

Bungie directly acknowledged the frustration surrounding Destiny 2--which received its last content update on June 9, 2026--including the removal of large amounts of content from the game in "sunsetting" processes.
"We haven't just heard your feedback. We understand the anger, the disappointment with us," Torkan said. "We're not asking for your trust, we know we have to earn it."
